scope: Read-only source/doc research, isolated native UI probe separately. No product edits, upload, receiver connection or personal browser profile.

findings.facts: The compatibility path accepts file URLs in addition to HTTP(S). Desktop remote-playback sources use Cast Streaming. Successful native connection requests playback and media remoting; the renderer has audio/video data pipes. This is a genuine browser transport path, not just a public file URL sent to the receiver.
findings.limitation: Opening a selector or a resolved prompt does not prove remote decoding.

findings.facts: Remote Playback discovery requires a valid video codec and a known remoting model. The native model predicate accepts names beginning Chromecast or Eureka Dongle, or exactly Google TV Streamer. Video/audio codecs are filtered separately. Names such as SHIELD, SHIELD Android TV and NVIDIA SHIELD do not satisfy that predicate.
findings.inference: A Shield exposing a Shield model name can appear in the ordinary Chrome Cast menu and detected-URL Default Media Receiver while being absent from the file Remote Playback selector.
findings.limitation: The actual user receiver advertised model_name has not been observed. The user supplied a receiver/product name, not the internal mDNS model field.

findings.topic: Global Media Controls does not provide TV tab fallback here
findings.facts: The API prompt opens the browser GMC device picker. Its preferred-mode chooser accepts Presentation or Remote Playback first; the TAB_MIRROR fallback is limited to audio-only sink icons CAST_AUDIO and CAST_AUDIO_GROUP. A TV lacking the supported Remote Playback mode is not rescued by that fallback.
findings.limitation: The ordinary toolbar Cast dialog has broader tab/screen choices and is a different entry point.

findings.facts: prompt checks transient user activation synchronously and also rejects detached windows, disabled backend, known unavailable devices or unsupported current source. The native connection-success code itself starts playback on desktop. Availability sources are disabled for duration at or below 15 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Do not await potentially slow play() before calling prompt inside a genuine click. Keep local media preparation distinct from requesting a receiver; asynchronous Save As or disk reads cannot be assumed to preserve a gesture indefinitely.
findings.limitation: A gesture fix does not remove the model/codec restrictions.

findings.facts: The backend is stable on Windows, Linux and macOS; media remoting without fullscreen is enabled by default there. Native remoting availability starts above 15 seconds; automatic fullscreen switching uses a separate 60-second threshold, and pixel-rate sampling uses five seconds. The extension should not change browser flags.

PresentationRequest accepts HTTP(S), cast and cast-dial schemes; internal tab-mirroring URNs and remote-playback schemes are not exposed by its constructor. Cast Streaming app IDs in either cast or legacy Google Cast URL forms are considered site-initiated mirroring and limited to the native origin allowlist unless a browser flag is changed.
findings.recommendation: Do not manufacture another origin or claim a raw mirroring app request bypasses these rules. A Default Media Receiver route alone cannot read a private PC file.

findings.facts: The current constants expose media-router-internals, access-code-cast and cast-feedback, not a generic chrome://media-router or chrome://cast picker. The former chrome://media-router dialog URL was removed in 2019.
findings.limitation: Access-code casting is a separate receiver-code flow, not the ordinary Shield picker.

findings.topic: A LAN HTTP server is not a drop-in extension permission
findings.facts: The sockets manifest feature is normally restricted to platform apps; its ordinary-extension branch has a narrow native allowlist. Alcydeo is not on that list. A normal MV3 desktop extension cannot simply add this permission to listen on a LAN TCP port.
findings.limitation: This does not rule out a separately installed companion/server or another application type; those change the confirmed scope.

conclusion.compatibleDeviceFilePath: A native file-backed HTML video plus RemotePlayback.prompt can use Chrome remoting on supported receiver models/codecs. Fix gesture/priming races and test a real supported receiver before claiming complete playback.
conclusion.knownShieldConstraint: A Shield model string does not match the pinned Remote Playback allowlist. No public extension API found that can remove this browser-side restriction or directly invoke the ordinary toolbar Cast tab dialog.
conclusion.bestAuthorizedFallback: Keep a playable local video in a persistent Alcydeo tab and give explicit instructions for Chrome menu Cast tab. This uses the user-confirmed working Shield menu path, stays local, and needs no duplicate disk copy just to mirror a Blob-backed local preview.
conclusion.changeOfScopeRequiredForOtherTransport: A default receiver needs a reachable media URL, or another receiver/transport. Adding a LAN companion/server, externally uploading the private file, or deploying a custom receiver would change the confirmed scope and cannot be silently introduced.
conclusion.factsVsUserInference: Browser-side model/codecs/picker restrictions are confirmed in the exact user Chrome156.0.8078.76 sources. The user actual model_name, exact runtime error and hardware route remain unobserved; this research must not be claimed as an end-to-end reproduction of that personal session.

redaction: No user cast token, task ID, file path, filename, device ID, LAN address, credentials or uploaded media in this report.

nativeUiProbe.limitations: No Windows graphical toolbar or physical receiver; parsing/navigation only. A fresh insecure about:blank does not expose PresentationRequest, so parsing was repeated in a secure inherited blank.
